gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-old-north: Noto Sans Old North Arabian reads dense and upright, its terminals flaring outward like the jaws of a pair of tongs. Edo SZ does its best work with one constant nib width, drafting-pen outlines with real stature, while the body just keeps its compact lowercase band steady.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-old-permi: Edo SZ draws its lowercase with the stature of cast iron capitals and never swells like a brush stroke. And Noto Sans Old Permic is the friendly counterweight, rounded and open to the side, its lowercase nearly matching capital height.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-old-persi: Noto Sans Old Persian reads lofty, its open counters breathing into the white space around them.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-old-sogdi: Noto Sans Old Sogdian reads crisp and approachable, its x-height climbing nearly to cap height with wide mouths that hold up when shrunk. Edo SZ holds one stroke width around every curve, as the body handles the small work.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-old-turki: Chunky, outlined, and unhurried. Noto Sans Old Turkic brings open-mouthed curves and a sturdy lowercase to meet Edo SZ, whose compass-pencil consistency gives the pair its strongest quality.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Edo SZ draws a plain, unshaded line that never swells. It makes a stately headline, and Noto Sans Oriya takes over below with generous gaps in its curves and small letters nearly matching the capitals.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-osage: Round, rimmed, and inflated. Edo SZ makes letters whose rims match their stems, and Noto Sans Osage follows with lowercase bowls that fill the line and sweeping curves that never close up.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-runic: Edo SZ looks like bent paperclip wire, with no thick-thin shifts anywhere. But Noto Sans Runic brings a big x-height and curves that never close back on themselves, so the two sit together with little friction.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-samaritan: Edo SZ keeps a calm, unvarying weight from word to word, which is what a display heading does best. And Noto Sans Samaritan, hefty in the lowercase with plenty of daylight inside its curves, is the sans-serif that carries the text.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-saurashtr: Cultural is the mood of Edo SZ, a heading drawn with the weight of a wire. Noto Sans Saurashtra is the clean sans-serif answer, its capitals barely taller than neighbors and its counters open to the outside.
